articles.title: The Model Is the Cheapest Part of Enterprise AI
articles.description: Why model access is the smallest cost in enterprise AI—and why workflow redesign, permissions, controls, and adoption determine banking ROI.

articles.title: The First Banking AI Winners Will Be Invisible
articles.description: Banking AI creates durable wins first in fraud, operations, engineering, and advisor workflows—the valuable work that customers never need to see.

articles.title: "Human in the Loop" Is Not a Governance Model
articles.description: Why a person in an AI workflow is not enough: effective human oversight requires defined authority, context, triggers, and response time at scale.

articles.title: When Every Bank Has the Same AI, What Still Matters?
articles.description: As AI models commoditize, banks will compete on context, permissions, workflow design, trust, and the institutional ability to learn faster.

articles.title: Your AI Agent Needs a Job Description
articles.description: AI agents in banking need explicit goals, authority, tools, escalation rules, and accountability before they can be trusted to perform real work safely.

articles.title: Your Bank Doesn’t Have a Data Problem. It Has a Permission Problem.
articles.description: The hardest bank data problem is often controlled access: who and what may see which information, for what purpose, and under which conditions.

articles.title: The First Wealth-Management AI Scandal Won’t Be a Hallucination
articles.description: The first wealth-management AI failure is more likely to be a suitability, incentive, or accountability problem than a spectacular hallucination.

articles.title: Banks Are Buying AI With Contracts Written for 2015
articles.description: Conventional software contracts miss AI model drift, data rights, agent authority, exit plans, fourth parties, and provider concentration risk.

articles.title: AI Will Make the Mass Affluent Worth Advising
articles.description: AI can make quality advice economical for mass-affluent clients—if firms redesign the advisor workflow without weakening suitability or trust.

articles.title: Banks Are Still Buying Software. AI Is Selling Them Labor.
articles.description: AI is changing enterprise software from seats and features into units of work. Banks must learn to buy outcomes without surrendering control.
